title: Chase Face ID & Biometrics Not Working? 4 Fast Solutions (iOS & Android) [2026]
content:
If you normally open the Chase Mobile App with a quick glance at your iPhone or a touch of your Android fingerprint sensor, having the app suddenly prompt you for your full username and password every time is an enormous annoyance.

Worse, when you navigate to the app settings to toggle Face ID or Fingerprint Login back on, you may encounter an error stating: **"Biometrics unavailable,"** or the switch immediately snaps back to the Off position.

Here is the exact technical reason why this occurs and the 4 surgical steps to fix it.

## Why Do Chase Biometrics Stop Working?

**Chase biometrics disable automatically when your device’s biometric cryptographic key desyncs from the app’s internal security keychain.** This happens whenever you add or alter a face/fingerprint in device settings, after major OS updates, or when your phone enters a low-power throttling state.

| Technical Parameter | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Platforms Affected** | Apple Face ID / Touch ID & Android BiometricPrompt |
| **Security Trigger** | Hardware Secure Enclave key rotation |
| **Common Trigger** | Registering an alternate appearance, system updates |
| **Fix Time** | Under 3 Minutes |

> 💡 **Quick Tip:** By banking security design, modifying ANY fingerprint or face data in your phone's main operating system automatically revokes biometric authorization across ALL banking apps to prevent unauthorized physical access.

## 4 Fast Solutions to Re-Enable Face ID and Fingerprints

Follow these streamlined solutions in order:

### 1. The "Clean Re-Pair" (Inside Chase Settings)
Attempting to toggle biometrics without first re-authenticating with your master password will always fail:
1. Manually type your username and password to log into the Chase app.
2. Tap the **Profile Icon** (person silhouette) in the top-right corner.
3. Tap **Sign-in & security**.
4. Tap **Face ID** (or **Fingerprint login**).
5. Toggle the switch **OFF**, wait 5 seconds, and toggle it **ON**.
6. When prompted, complete your biometric scan. This provisions a fresh encryption certificate.

### 2. Verify iOS / Android System-Level App Permissions
If Chase does not have permission from Apple or Google to query your biometric sensors:
* **For iPhone (iOS):**
  1. Open iPhone **Settings**.
  2. Scroll down to the installed apps list and select **Chase**.
  3. Verify that the **Face ID** toggle is enabled (green). If it was off, turn it on and relaunch Chase.
* **For Android:**
  1. Open phone **Settings** > **Security & privacy** > **Biometrics**.
  2. Ensure **Biometric unlock** is active.
  3. Go to **Settings** > **Apps** > **Chase** > **Permissions** and confirm biometric sensors are permitted.

> 💡 **Related Chase Bank Solution:** Encountering related issues? Check our verified fix for [Chase App Not Working After Update: How to Fix App Store & Play Store Update Loops](/guides/chase-app-not-working-after-update).


### 3. Clear the Secure Enclave Cache via Hard Reboot
If your phone's biometric daemon process is hung in memory:
* **iPhone (Face ID models):** Press and release Volume Up, press and release Volume Down, then hold the Power button until the Apple logo appears.
* **Android:** Hold the Power button and tap **Restart**.
*A cold boot restarts the hardware biometric enclave and clears stale sensor handles.*

### 4. Reinstall App to Flush Corrupted Keychain Entries
If the Chase app continues to forget your biometric preference after device reboots:
1. Delete the Chase app completely from your home screen.
2. Restart your smartphone.
3. Re-download **Chase Mobile** from the App Store or Google Play.
4. Sign in manually once, and when the prompt asks **"Enable Face ID / Fingerprint for future logins?"**, tap **Allow**.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Does toggling Face ID off and on change my banking password?**
**No.** Biometric login is simply an encrypted local shortcut stored on your device. Your underlying Chase username and password remain completely unaffected.

**Why does Chase ask for a one-time [verification code](/guides/chase-not-sending-otp-verification-text) when I re-enable biometrics?**
**Because pairing a biometric sensor with your bank account is considered a high-security action.** Chase sends a two-factor SMS to confirm that the legitimate account owner is authorizing the device.

**What should I do if my camera hardware works but Face ID fails across all apps?**
**If Face ID fails across your entire iPhone (including unlocking your phone), your TrueDepth camera sensor may require Apple hardware diagnostics.** Contact Apple Support or schedule a Genius Bar appointment.
